issues.description: Ingest is not atomic; parser failures can leave partial new results committed with cleared or missing stats.
Ingest clears warnings/stats but never clears results, so rows from prior input directories remain stale.
Harness B parser assumes JSONL records and metrics are objects; arrays, strings, or bad metrics crash with AttributeError.
Score parsing accepts NaN as a float, then SQLite insertion fails the NOT NULL constraint instead of recording a warning.
Malformed Harness C XML raises ParseError and aborts ingestion instead of being handled as a data-quality problem.
Untrusted XML is parsed with stdlib ElementTree rather than a hardened parser such as defusedxml.
Harness A reads by column position and ignores the header, so reordered CSV columns are silently mis-ingested.
Required fields like run_id, model, and task can be empty strings and still be inserted as valid rows.
Harness A metadata accepts any JSON type, so raw_extra can be an array despite the documented metadata-object contract.
stderr parsing accepts non-finite floats such as NaN or Infinity instead of rejecting or warning.
Report opens missing database paths with connect(), creating an empty database and masking path/configuration mistakes.
Fixture generation recursively deletes the requested output directory without safety checks.
Tests cover generated fixtures but miss malformed inputs, transaction rollback, stale-row behavior, and non-finite numbers.
